items.title: Japanese court says voice is protected by publicity rights; US appeals court says AI training is not fair use
items.summary: There have been two judgments this week of relevance to the ongoing AI debates in the music industry. A Japanese court ruled that publicity rights allow performers to stop unapproved AI voice clones. Meanwhile a US appeals court ruled against an AI company that used the good old fair use defence

items.title: ‘The Song Is Non-Negotiable’: Indie Music Giants Unite to Force a Fair Licensing Framework
items.summary: Indie publishing orgs IMPF and IMPEL have outlined a licensing framework for generative AI to create a fair and sustainable market for the future. Independent music publishing organizations IMPEL and IMPF have now issued a licensing framework for generative AI based on several key principles that will ensure song copyr…

items.title: Suno Blasts Latest UMG/Sony Lawsuit As ‘Fundamentally Flawed on Both the Facts and the Law’
items.summary: UMG and Sony file another copyright lawsuit against Suno, and the AI company claps back with a statement that the suit is “fundamentally flawed.” Universal Music Group and Sony Music Entertainment continue to heat things up in their ongoing legal battle against the AI music platform Suno. items.title: Trump’s DoJ was biased and wrong about ‘fair use’, say news orgs in OpenAI dispute
items.summary: Many of the music industry’s AI legal battles swing on whether or not AI training is ‘fair use’ under US copyright law. Donald Trump’s DoJ recently intervened in a dispute between newspapers and OpenAI insisting AI training is fair use. The newspapers have responded, explaining why the DoJ is wrong

ElevenLabs valuation doubles to $22B – four times that of AI music rival Suno
items.summary: ElevenLabs completed a USD $300 million employee tender offer at a valuation of $22 billion. Source

items.title: Suno is ‘far beyond’ 2m subscribers and $300m of annual revenue
items.summary: It’s been a little while since AI-music firm Suno announced its user and revenue stats. We’re not getting new figures just yet, but CEO Mikey Shulman provided an update of sorts in an interview with Bloomberg. The post is from Music Ally .

items.title: Kelly Clarkson Says ‘I Love AI’ but AI Artists Should Not Be on the Same Music Charts as Humans
items.summary: Kelly Clarkson has shared her admittedly “controversial” opinion on artificial intelligence, saying she thinks it can do “amazing things” but shouldn’t be able to create anything that competes with humans, particularly on music charts. The pop star shared her feelings about the technology during an appearance on the La…

items.title: IMPF and IMPEL publish AI licensing principles, insisting songs and recordings must be valued equally
items.summary: As the music industry enters into ever more deals with AI platforms, the indie publisher community has again insisted that - with AI - song rights and recording rights must be valued equally, unlike in streaming. A new AI framework from IMPF and IMPEL says that key principle is “non-negotiable”

tip.title: Registra tu catálogo también en la sociedad de gestión
tip.body: El registro de autoría y la recaudación son trámites distintos. Si tu obra no está dada de alta en la sociedad correspondiente, las regalías de ejecución pública simplemente no te llegan.

tip.title: Register with your collecting society too
tip.body: Copyright registration and royalty collection are separate steps. If your work isn't registered with the right society, public performance royalties simply never reach you.
